metadata.goal: Assess whether one user has stable individual mobility preferences across repeated trips, and whether those preferences change with trip purpose.
metadata.category: Single-user repeated routes, mode-conditioned speed behaviour, and purpose-conditioned routine stability
metadata.header: MTL Trajet: 05 Single User Purpose Habits
metadata.dataset_description: A constructed single-user case derived from MTL Trajet geometry and purpose/mode context. Work trips share a repeated corridor. All supplied route vertices are retained during resampling; shopping trip _054 uses a cached OSRM road route. Point speeds have within-mode variation, and timestamps integrate the delivered segment distances and speeds. Trip mean speed is distance divided by duration; point_speed_mean_kmh is the unweighted point mean. Conflicting trip dates are reconstructed to remove single-user time overlaps while preserving local departure times and weekdays; source_start_time and calendar_shift_days record the changes.
metadata.metric_note: `longest_stable_run_points` is the longest consecutive GPS-point segment whose adjacent speed changes stay within the mode-specific limit recorded in `stable_speed_change_threshold_kmh`: walking 0.15, cycling 0.25, public transit 0.40, and motor vehicle 0.60 km/h. This local continuity metric is distinct from full-trajectory `point_speed_std_kmh`.
metadata.source_note: Historical trajectories (2016) are spatially matched to the 2025 official PUM land-use taxonomy; do not interpret the categories as historical 2016 land-use observations.

insight_list.question: Within each transport mode, does this user retain comparable typical speed levels and similar acceleration/deceleration rhythms despite different purposes and distances?
insight_list.code:
grid = np.linspace(0,1,101)
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1,3,figsize=(16,4.8),constrained_layout=True)
modes=['walking','cycling','public_transit','motor_vehicle']
colors=['#16a34a','#7c3aed','#0f766e','#ea580c']
axes[0].boxplot([df[df.mode_group.eq(m)].avg_speed_kmh for m in modes],tick_labels=[m.replace('_',' ') for m in modes])
axes[0].set(title='Typical trip speeds within each mode',ylabel='trip mean speed (km/h)');axes[0].tick_params(axis='x',rotation=25)
for mode,color in zip(modes,colors):
    profiles=[]; accelerations=[]
    for _,g in user_df[user_df.mode_group.eq(mode)].groupby('trajectory_id'):
        g=g.sort_values('point_index'); times=pd.to_datetime(g.timestamp,format='mixed'); seconds=(times-times.iloc[0]).dt.total_seconds().to_numpy(); progress=seconds/seconds[-1]
        v=g.speed_kmh.to_numpy(); acceleration=np.diff(v)/3.6/np.diff(seconds)
        profiles.append(np.interp(grid,progress,v));accelerations.append(np.interp(grid,(progress[1:]+progress[:-1])/2,acceleration))
    for ax,data in [(axes[1],profiles),(axes[2],accelerations)]:
        values=np.array(data); ax.fill_between(grid,np.quantile(values,.1,axis=0),np.quantile(values,.9,axis=0),color=color,alpha=.15)
        ax.plot(grid,np.median(values,axis=0),color=color,label=mode.replace('_',' '));ax.grid(alpha=.2)
axes[1].set(title='Within-mode speed rhythms (median, 10–90%)',xlabel='fraction of elapsed trip time',ylabel='speed (km/h)')
axes[2].set(title='Acceleration derived from speed and time',xlabel='fraction of elapsed trip time',ylabel='acceleration (m/s²)')
axes[1].legend(fontsize=8);axes[2].axhline(0,color='gray',lw=.7)
print(df.groupby('mode_group').avg_speed_kmh.agg(['mean','std','min','max']).round(3))
plt.show()

insights: This user repeatedly follows the same work-related corridor, with several work trajectories passing through the same road-area sequence; shopping and leisure trajectories are spatially more dispersed.

Even when trip distance and destination differ, this user's trajectories retain comparable typical speed levels and similar acceleration/deceleration rhythms within the same transport mode; the profiles change clearly when the mode changes.
The user's routine work and education trips have more stable departure times and transport modes, while shopping, dining, and leisure trips vary more in departure time, mode, and trajectory length.
summary: This single-user history contains a repeated work commute corridor and mode-consistent point-speed profiles. Work and education are routine-like in time and mode, whereas shopping, dining, and leisure cover more varied times, modes, destinations, and distances.
evidence_policy: Claims describe patterns in this dataset and do not establish causal relationships.
